title: Session cache priority inversion exposes org-scoped requests to wrong tenant during high-load reconnects
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary: During an edge reconnect scenario under bursty traffic, the in-memory session cache exhibited a priority inversion that allowed a stale tenant binding to be served for unrelated requests. This resulted in intermittent authorization misbindings (requests being evaluated under the wrong org scope) across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. A Dedicated customer (AcmePay) escalated after observing failed transactions and denied operations tied to incorrect tenant scoping.

Why this matters: Cross-tenant authorization errors are high-severity (data confidentiality and correctness). The bug is a production reliability and security risk; customers reported financial impact and required immediate remediation.

This ticket tracks the investigation, mitigation, fix, release, and postmortem tasks. It contains repro steps, timeline, root cause, and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a dedicated cluster with edge-proxy and session-service; seed two tenants (org-A and org-B) with active API keys.

2) From a reproducible harness, open long-lived websocket-like connections via edge-proxy and send interleaved requests from org-A and org-B: a stream of requests from org-A, then trigger a simulated connection reconnect on the edge (TCP teardown) and immediately issue a burst of requests for org-B.

3) Observe session-service logs: under high concurrency the cache slot used for org-A can be evicted and replaced by org-B, but race on header validation allows a small window where requests still carry org-A session metadata while cache slot now maps to org-B; authz lookup uses stale metadata leading to mis-evaluation.

4) Trigger with traffic shape similar to customer production (p95 payload sizes, keepalive intervals) to reproduce nondeterministic but deterministic in our harness when concurrency >= 200 and reconnect frequency > 1/min.
5) Reproducer and harness are checked into ci: drive/si/repro/session-priority-inversion.tar.gz and internal test job session-cache-inversion-cts.
impact: Several customers experienced intermittent authorization failures: some requests accepted when they should be rejected, and vice versa; billing/transaction flows for one Dedicated customer failed at times. Incidents were reported in Hosted, Dedicated, and an on-prem Private deployment (via partner), indicating the bug exists in the common session-service runtime used across deployments.

root_cause: A priority inversion bug in the session-cache fast-path: when a cache entry was evicted and replaced concurrently while an edge reconnect was replaying buffered requests, the session-service's fast-path assumed slot ownership and returned the newly written entry without verifying the original request's tenant header. The combination of (1) aggressive cache slot reuse, (2) a non-atomic update path for tenant tags, and (3) the edge-proxy's buffered replay of requests during reconnect created a small timing window where request-scoped tenant metadata and cached tenant tag diverged. This allowed authz lookups to be performed with stale binding.
mitigation:
1) Short-term: Disabled session-cache fast-path behind FF on edge-proxy and increased sync interval so replayed requests revalidate token binding. This was applied to affected clusters first.
2) Medium-term: Deploy hotfix to session-service with atomic compare-and-swap per cache slot and explicit tenant-tag validation.
3) Communication: Notified affected customers (AcmePay and two Hosted customers) and provided patch packages for Private deployments.
resolution: PR merged and backported to 1.26 branch. Changes: (a) atomic CAS for cache slot replace, (b) tenant-tag attached to cache entry and verified against request header before returning fast-path result, (c) additional metrics for cache evictions and tenant-mismatch events. Edge-proxy now rejects buffered replay requests if tenant header no longer matches slot tag. Hotfix deployed to staging (2026-03-13) and rolled to prod (2026-03-14 HOTFIX).

postmortem_tasks: 1) Complete formal postmortem doc in Confluence: confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/ENG-621579-postmortem
2) Add unit + integration tests covering reconnect + cache eviction race; add CI job that runs reproducer under stress.
3) Instrument additional metrics: tenant-mismatch-count, cache-slot-cas-failure, replayed-request-rejections.
4) Run a one-week canary across Dedicated customers with increased sampling and validate no regressions.
5) Update runbook & incident response docs to include session-cache hot-path FF and checklist to apply to Private appliances.
6) Customer follow-up: schedule 1:1 with AcmePay engineering and account team to review incident and confirm residual risk is acceptable.
7) Security follow-up: provide exported audit logs for affected window and file required compliance notices where applicable.
8) Retrospective: evaluate if cache namespace sharding per-tenant should be default to reduce any future tenant-binding windows.
9) Close ticket once postmortem reviewed and follow-ups either completed or tracked as separate issues.
